races.name: Book Tickets Online At www.corkracecourse.ie Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Aiteall
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for O'Brien who fades late; 10 days since last run is a positive freshness angle, but a tendency to weaken in the closing stages limits confidence unless pace is strong enough to compress the finish.|

runners_data.name: Glamazon
runners_data.note: Harrington-trained hold-up filly with the best sim-going record in the field (13/15 runs on similar ground, 1W 4P); races towards the rear but has placed consistently on Good ground and is best suited if she can secure a prominent enough position given how congested the back of this field will be.|

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: Honest hold-up type who has placed on multiple occasions on Good ground and over today's trip; racing out of her most natural role given the crowded rear, so getting a position just off the mid-pack rather than at the back will be key to her chance.|

runners_data.name: Oppenheimer
runners_data.note: Coleman-trained hold-up runner with zero wins or places from six runs on similar ground; no obvious tactical advantage in this shape, and the consistently poor record on Good-type surfaces makes this one hard to recommend.|

runners_data.name: Sunrise Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly from Slattery's yard with two places on similar ground from nine attempts; has shown enough to suggest she stays the mile, but the crowded rear of this field means she is unlikely to get the clean run her style depends on.|

runners_data.name: Tenacious
runners_data.note: Harrington runner whose true style is as a prominent racer, redistributed to midfield here because the field is simply too hold-up heavy to show that at the rear; should be noted she fades in the finish, and racing out of role at STYLE_FIT 0.90 softens her claims considerably.|

runners_data.name: Beau Army
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and pivot of the entire race shape; McGuinness has had four winners from 24 runners over 14 days, and Beau Army's recent win over 7f on Good ground shows he can handle conditions — everything depends on whether he can replicate that performance over an extra furlong.|

runners_data.name: Ochtar Againn
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is at the back, but the depth of hold-up types here means Harnett will be forced to race closer than ideal — no wins from eight runs on Good ground, and racing out of character at STYLE_FIT 0.90 dims the outlook.|

runners_data.name: Sceitimini
runners_data.note: All five of her starts have come at sprint trips (5-6f) on Good or Yielding ground; she fades late and her entire form has been at shorter distances, so the step up to a mile on Good to Yielding looks a significant ask beyond the positional compression issue.|

runners_data.name: Miss Ivor
runners_data.note: A hold-up type with a worrying tendency to fade in the closing stages; consistently finishing mid-to-rear in six starts, none on today's trip, and her redistribution out of a natural rear position into the mid-pack further reduces a chance that was already marginal.|

runners_data.name: Sayonara
runners_data.note: The most likely horse to press Beau Army for the prominent berth; placed twice on Good ground and her best recent run was a 2nd over 7f, suggesting she stays this trip — if she can lead or at least race on Beau Army's girth, she represents the clearest danger to the front-runner.|

runners_data.name: Arizona Star
runners_data.note: Mulvany-trained hold-up runner returning from a 53-day break who has placed on three occasions on similar ground; the step down from longer trips (10-12f) to a mile is interesting and worth noting, but racing out of role in a congested field is a mitigating factor.|

runners_data.name: Cause I Like You
runners_data.note: Has a win and two places on Good-type ground at this trip for Mulvany and possesses the most compelling recent form figures of the hold-up group; her natural position is at the back, but she is redistributed into mid-pack and STYLE_FIT 0.92 means the scenario where she delivers late needs things to fall right.|

runners_data.name: Thumama Sands
runners_data.note: Four runs, all on Good ground, all at 7f, all resulting in finishes of 9th or worse — the combination of stepping up in trip and a persistent tendency to fade in the finish makes this one of the least encouraging profiles in the field.|

runners_data.name: Due In June
runners_data.note: Has not run for 59 days and has never finished better than 6th from five starts on Good ground; a hold-up type who fades late, and the absence combined with a poor record in similar conditions makes her hard to support even in a wide-open handicap.|

runners_data.name: Garryowen Green
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated horse in the field at OR 40, but has shown ability to place on Good ground at 7f and the step up to a mile should suit on pedigree; racing out of role as a redistributed hold-up type, though her record of placing suggests she could be a longer-priced factor if luck runs her way.|

races.paceDynamic: Beau Army is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the early lead, Sam Coen can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Yielding ground around Cork's flat mile. The pace will be honest but not scorching — a single leader at the head of affairs over a mile on this surface typically sets up a race that rewards those travelling prominently just behind, close enough to respond when the tempo lifts in the final two furlongs. Sayonara is the one horse likely to press Beau Army for the prominent berth, with Glamazon and Dawn Flame best positioned among the hold-up types to challenge from a ground-saving position. The field holds significantly more genuine hold-up horses than the rear of the field can accommodate — Tenacious, Sceitimini, Ochtar Againn, Miss Ivor, Cause I Like You and others are natural closers who will be shuffled further back than ideal, meaning the race shape firmly favours horses able to race prominently or in the first half of the field, as the late closers face a difficult task coming from compressed positions without a truly searching pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beau Army Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Beau Army is allowed to stride clear uncontested and sets a measured, even tempo that suits a prominent racer kicking on from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Beau Army dictates every yard, the pace is sustainable rather than punishing, and those racing just behind in Sayonara's company are best placed to pounce; horses from deep in the field simply have too much ground to make up without a fast early gallop to exploit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Duel Home
scenarios.trigger: If Sayonara tracks Beau Army closely and the two race in tandem setting a stronger pace, bringing the field into play entering the straight.
scenarios.body: A genuine duel between the two prominent types elevates the pace enough to compress the gaps, allowing a horse like Glamazon or Dawn Flame travelling just off them to swoop; the extra pressure stretches Beau Army but improves the chances of the second-rank prominent runners.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the front two tire in the final furlong and a well-positioned hold-up runner finds a clear run through.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a faster-than-expected tempo and a perfectly timed run, conditions that are far from guaranteed given the compressed nature of the rear group and the redistributed closers racing out of role; Cause I Like You and Aiteall have the form to benefit if the gaps open.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse And Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Beau Army goes overly easy and the field concertinas entering the straight, turning the race into a short-dash sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A lack of true pace produces a bunched, messy finish where positional luck and draw become dominant factors; Arizona Star and Garryowen Green, who have shown ability to place when traffic clears, are the wildcards in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Sayonara — watch whether Adam Browne-Souza pushes forward immediately from the gate to lock in the prominent position behind Beau Army; if she secures that berth, she becomes the primary danger to the front-runner entering the straight.|

Beau Army — if Sam Coen allows a slower-than-expected pace, the field will bunch dramatically entering the final two furlongs and Beau Army's advantage evaporates; monitor the early splits from the front.|

Glamazon — Darragh O'Sullivan (7) will need to make a decision early about whether to push forward from a natural hold-up position; if she gets lost in the congested rear group, her strong going record becomes irrelevant.|

Cause I Like You — her record of 1W 2P on Good-type ground at today's trip is the most relevant piece of form among the back-of-the-field runners, and if there is any pace collapse or late compression, she is the likeliest beneficiary of any situation where gaps open.|

Sceitimini — having raced exclusively at 5-6f, this is a significant step up in distance; watch whether she settles in the early stages, as a horse who has only ever raced at sprint trips could take a strong hold and empty quickly in the final quarter-mile.|

races.name: Glenvale Stud Race

runners_data.name: Benevento
runners_data.note: Won last time at 8f on Good and has placed repeatedly at 7f; W J Lee adds class in the saddle, prominent style suits this controlled shape, and 23 days since last run is a fresh prep — solid each-way claims.|

runners_data.name: Felix Guido
runners_data.note: Won three on the bounce earlier in his career but returns after 125 days off with a known tendency to fade in the finish; Joseph Patrick O'Brien's 12/71 14-day trainer strike rate is notable but the layoff and the fade flag make him difficult to trust at a tight market price.|

runners_data.name: Bold Style
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery, which is an unusual angle to note; genuine hold-up performer whose 8-from-10 similar-going record speaks well, but Cork's 7f is unlikely to see the strong pace he needs to produce his best late effort.|

runners_data.name: Gleneagle Bay
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on Good and has five placings in similar conditions from 15 starts, making him the most course-and-conditions reliable hold-up runner in the field; the 3lb claim for Jack Kearney helps at the weights and he is the stand-out closer if this race breaks open.|

runners_data.name: Inventor
runners_data.note: An 847-day absence is an enormous flag for this nine-year-old returning from nearly two and a half years off; though a natural hold-up performer, forced into midfield by field congestion, and the combination of layoff and compromised position makes a winning contribution extremely unlikely.|

runners_data.name: Bamako Beach
runners_data.note: The highest-profile hold-up to prominent runner here on form — won last time at 7f on Good and has placed in all four starts on similar going; Seamie Heffernan's record and M D O'Callaghan's 1/11 recent trainer form temper enthusiasm slightly, but this horse's profile suits the dominant race shape most cleanly.|

runners_data.name: Res Ipsa
runners_data.note: Colin Keane on a G M Lyons-trained front-runner who has won and placed at 8f on Good is the confirmed pace-setter; can dictate unanswered and the 48-day freshener may sharpen him, though he is a 3-year-old stepping into a competitive handicap from the front.|

runners_data.name: Roaring Fire
runners_data.note: A striking 120 OR on debut win at 6f on Soft but has not run for 346 days and races in blinkers for the first time over a trip longer than his sole start; the layoff and the unknown stamina profile at 7f make him a speculative but fascinating inclusion for O'Callaghan.|

runners_data.name: Bella Isabella
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes takes the mount for Dermot Weld, whose patient handling of this mare is reflected in her two wins; proven at 7f on Soft and her hold-up style gives her a live shout if the race develops chaotically, though the 52-day gap and a mixed recent form string (07-015) introduce some doubt.|

races.paceDynamic: Res Ipsa is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, ridden by Colin Keane for G M Lyons, is likely to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable clip on Good To Yielding ground over 7f at Cork. The prominent cluster — Benevento, Felix Guido, Bamako Beach, and Roaring Fire — will all press to secure early positions just off the leader, creating genuine congestion and potential interference in the first two furlongs before the field strings out. Hold-up types Gleneagle Bay, Bold Style, Bella Isabella, and the redistributed Inventor will be forced to settle in behind that scrum, with the latter unlikely to find the deep cover and late run it needs given the limited genuine pace ahead. This race shape — a controlled lead at steady-to-moderate tempo with a prominent group tracking closely — overwhelmingly favours prominent racers who can travel economically and produce a finish from a stalking position, rather than hold-up horses dependent on a strong early gallop to close into. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate cleanly; of those vying for early position, Bamako Beach and Res Ipsa are best placed to actually secure their natural roles given their class and rider quality.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Res Ipsa dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent challengers track without incident
scenarios.body: Res Ipsa sets a sustainable tempo under Colin Keane and the race becomes a test of class and finishing kick from the front rank from the 2f pole; prominent horses who travel smoothly into contention are perfectly positioned to pounce when the pace steadies. Bamako Beach, with strong similar-going form and a top jockey, and Benevento, who has placed at this trip repeatedly, are the chief beneficiaries of this controlled shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Gaps Open Late
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent types clash for position early and the pace surges irregularly before settling
scenarios.body: The early battle for berths behind Res Ipsa causes uneven fractions, burning energy from Felix Guido and Roaring Fire and creating openings for hold-up horses as the field fans out 2f from home. Gleneagle Bay, proven at this trip and going with a strong 12-from-15 similar-going record, and Bella Isabella, a genuine hold-up type with a win at 7f on soft, are positioned to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Roaring Fire Bolt, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Fire and Res Ipsa push the early tempo and the race develops into a true test of stamina at the trip
scenarios.body: Roaring Fire, a 120-rated horse with a single but emphatic win, fires from prominent and joins Res Ipsa to inject genuine pace that rewards those who can sustain their effort to the line; the race becomes a test of resolution rather than finishing speed. Bamako Beach's strong 4-from-4 similar-going record and Res Ipsa's course-proven composure make them the likeliest to outlast the field if the gallop is genuine.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Arrive Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entering the final furlong and deep hold-up horses produce a late rattle
scenarios.body: Bold Style and Gleneagle Bay would be the nominal beneficiaries of a scenario where the prominent pack ties up, but this shape is heavily discounted because Inventor — the truest hold-up type in the field — is racing well out of role and cannot be expected to deliver a genuine late challenge from its forced midfield position. Even if closers arrive, the gap between them and the leaders is unlikely to be bridged at Cork's 7f unless the early pace was genuinely fierce.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic trouble 2-3 furlongs out as Benevento, Felix Guido, Bamako Beach, and Roaring Fire all target the same prominent positions behind Res Ipsa — any significant crowding here could unwind the chances of the most market-fancied runners.

Roaring Fire's 346-day absence and blinkers application for the first time is an immediate flag — monitor his pre-race demeanour and early behaviour in the stalls, as an unruly or detached start could compromise the entire prominent group around him.

Felix Guido's "fades in finish" tag combined with a 125-day layoff means Shay Wallace must balance holding a prominent position against burning his horse out early — if he goes too soon from the front rank, he could fatally compromise those tucked in behind.

Inventor's 847-day return means watch for any signs of greenness or reluctance in the parade ring and early stages; even as a redistributed midfield runner, an erratic run could cause interference for Bold Style and Gleneagle Bay coming from behind.|

Cork's 7f track tends to favour those who can slot in behind the pace and produce a clean run from 2f out — jockeys on Gleneagle Bay and Bella Isabella should be watched for whether they manage to find clear daylight on the home turn without cover problems.|

races.name: Coolmore Stud Little Big Bear Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Catalina Delcarpio
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Pat Twomey with W J Lee up; 74 days off but her form reads well on similar going (5 of 6 recent runs on Good-plus), and her two wins are both at 8f, so dropping back to 7f is a slight query though she has placed at the trip.

runners_data.name: Greydreambeliever
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose last five runs are all at 7f; the redistribution here masks her true rearward position, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 and only two placed efforts in fifteen similar-going runs she faces a stiff ask racing outside her comfort zone in midfield.

runners_data.name: Princess Child
runners_data.note: True closer for the powerful Joseph O'Brien yard; headgear flagged, but her recent form over 7f is poor (two 11th-place finishes) and being displaced further forward than ideal does her no favours given her tendency to need things to fall right late.

runners_data.name: Stugardia
runners_data.note: Returning from a lengthy 329-day break for O'Brien; hold-up profile but all five recent runs have come on Soft or Yielding and at longer trips (8f-11f), so the step back to 7f on Good To Yielding is a significant question mark on comeback.

runners_data.name: Wannabe Royal
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead prominent type who won over 7f on Good 80 days ago; the layoff is mild concern but he has form on soft ground and will be competitive close to the pace if fresh enough, though his 6f efforts show he can be one-paced.

runners_data.name: Cromac Quay
runners_data.note: Won his only start over 7f on Soft for Harrington, with placed efforts over 8f on Good — a progressive three-year-old who handles the conditions, gets Shane Foley, and the compact record (three runs only) suggests a horse still on the upgrade in this grade.

runners_data.name: Dancing Saxon
runners_data.note: Lively fresh-legged runner for O'Brien, racing just seven days ago; has won over 7f on Good and his form string of 11213 shows admirable consistency, though a hold-up profile in a race where the map has pushed him toward midfield means he needs luck in running.

runners_data.name: Josh's Joy
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Donnacha O'Brien who handles this going and distance; 105 days off is a notable absence, and while his last two runs at 7f on Soft/Good were placed, his sprint at 6f suggests he may not fully see out the 7f in a tactical race where he needs to be close.

runners_data.name: Magny Cours
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for McLoughlin with Ben Coen; four placed efforts in nine similar-going runs with only one win, and 98 days since his last run adds another layer of doubt, though his course form over 7f-8f gives him a valid profile if the pace truly heats up late.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Attack
runners_data.note: Prominent racer one day since last run — an unusually short turnaround — for Murphy with Heffernan in the saddle; won over 7f on Soft and has placed at Group level, but that recency of effort combined with a mixed recent record (8th, 4th, 8th flanking a win) makes his form volatile.

runners_data.name: Prevalence
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse for G M Lyons with Colin Keane; headgear noted (p), and while Keane's booking is always significant, his redistribution to midfield (STYLE_FIT 0.92) means he is racing outside his instinctive position — discount his chance unless the race genuinely develops into a strong-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Spinning Around
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien runner whose last five starts confirm a hold-up profile, yet the field density forces her to a midfield mapping (STYLE_FIT 0.93); headgear flagged, she won over 7f on Good and handles the going, but being displaced closer to the pace than suits is a real tactical handicap here.

runners_data.name: Suzie Songs
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field; four wins from eight starts on Good going over 7f for G M Lyons and Gary Carroll, and the combination of an uncontested lead and suitable going makes her the pivotal race-shaper — her ability to control tempo is the single most important factor in determining how this race unfolds.

runners_data.name: Wild Bessie
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for De Bromhead with Lordan; only one win from four starts on varied ground with no placed effort on similar going in this analysis, and the redistribution to midfield (STYLE_FIT 0.92) compounds the challenge — best watched rather than relied upon at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Suzie Songs is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 14-strong field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Gary Carroll can dictate a comfortable, unhurried gallop from the front on going that is Good To Yielding throughout the card at Cork. The prominent types — Catalina Delcarpio, Wannabe Royal, Cromac Quay, Josh's Joy and Pivotal Attack — will sit just off the pace, but with no rival willing or able to force the issue, the early tempo is firmly in Suzie Songs' control. Several horses labelled here as midfield are in reality hold-up types — Spinning Around, Prevalence, Greydreambeliever and Wild Bessie — redistributed forward on the map because the field carries more closers than the shape can accommodate at the rear, meaning their true tactical position will be further back than shown and their chance in a shape that requires midfield positioning is tempered. A single, uncontested front-runner setting a moderate pace on soft-ish ground strongly favours horses that sit close to the pace and pounce at the two-furlong pole, rather than those relying on a strong late gallop from off the bridle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Suzie Songs Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Suzie Songs is allowed a solo lead at a measured tempo and the prominent horses cannot collar her in the straight.
scenarios.body: Suzie Songs has won both her last two starts over 7f on Good ground and, with no pace rival to press her, Gary Carroll can set a rhythm that plays entirely to her strengths; on Good To Yielding the moderate gallop will keep the race well within her stamina range and a clean exit from the stalls seals it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly moderate and one of the well-positioned prominent runners finds a fresher gear to overhaul Suzie Songs inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A genuine moderate pace with 14 runners means Cromac Quay or Catalina Delcarpio, sitting just off the leader's flank, can time their challenge to land a decisive blow as the front-runner's reserves thin on the softish surface; Cromac Quay's recent win over this course configuration and Catalina Delcarpio's consistency at this level make both credible threats.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than anticipated — perhaps Josh's Joy or Pivotal Attack pressing Suzie Songs — and the race sets up for a strong finisher.
scenarios.body: A genuinely run race over 7f on Good To Yielding ground can open a lane for a closer, but the horses best placed to exploit it — Spinning Around, Prevalence and Greydreambeliever — are true hold-up types being mapped to midfield under redistribution, meaning they face the double burden of traffic and an unfamiliar position; Dancing Saxon, who has been running prominently with sharp tactical speed, is the most credible beneficiary if late closers are rewarded.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types refuse to settle, the field bunches in midfield and the race becomes a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: With 14 runners, a crowded midfield and genuine hold-up horses shuffled into unnatural positions, interference and checking in the straight is a live risk; in that scrambled finish, a horse with sharp acceleration rather than pure stamina benefits, and Pivotal Attack or Josh's Joy — both carrying tactical speed and positioned to seize any gap — emerge as the likeliest profiteers.

watchPoints.text: Suzie Songs — watch her stall exit and first 100 yards; if she misses the break or a prominent rival pins her immediately, the entire race shape inverts and prominent types rather than the leader become the default winners.

Pivotal Attack — racing just one day after his last start is unusually aggressive scheduling; watch for any signs of flatness or reluctance early, as a below-par effort from a supposed prominent racer could compress the midfield dangerously in a 14-runner field.

Cromac Quay — three runs only, still lightly raced and improving; if Shane Foley slots him cleanly onto Suzie Songs' quarters from a handy draw, he becomes the most dangerous late challenge to the leader rather than a straightforward second-string runner.

Spinning Around, Prevalence, Greydreambeliever and Wild Bessie — all true closers forced into midfield on the map; watch whether jockeys actually push them forward at the start or accept their natural hold-up berth, as their finishing position will reveal whether the redistribution reflects reality.

Going confirmation — all races at Cork today are Good To Yielding, not the Good listed in the race conditions; any further watering or shower activity could tip the balance toward stamina-heavy profiles and away from Suzie Songs if the ground becomes genuinely testing.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Abergwaun Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Kendall Roy
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a strong 5f record on good ground (sim-going 15/15) and a recent course-level win; Chris Hayes rides and this horse's prominent style suits a race where securing a clean position just off Rosie Frith would be ideal, though the four-way prominent scramble is the key risk to a smooth trip.

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up specialist with consistent 5f form on similar going (sim-going 14/15) but has been winless over the trip in recent starts; Gary Carroll will need a strong pace to materialise for this horse's late run to land, which the race shape makes unlikely.

runners_data.name: Brussels
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien three-year-old ridden by Wayne Lordan; recent form is modest (no win since debut) and the prominent style faces a congested battle for position, with the step back to 5f on yielding ground an unknown given most recent starts at 6f.

runners_data.name: Gazelle d'Or
runners_data.note: Hold-up four-year-old with a solid placed record at 5f on good ground (4W9P, sim-going 14/15) and a lengthy break of 86 days; W J Lee will be looking for a stronger pace than this race is likely to generate, and the layoff requires monitoring.

runners_data.name: Likedbymike
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride on this four-year-old who won over 6f recently and has consistent 5f placed form; a genuine prominent runner with a legitimate claim to a position just off the leader, and the Keane booking is an upgrade on connections' recent jockey use.

runners_data.name: Sarahmae
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type who has won over 5f on soft ground and has three wins in recent form; J M Sheridan rides and the yielding conditions are a genuine plus, though the race shape needs to produce more pace than expected for this horse to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Cardiff By The Sea
runners_data.note: J A Stack three-year-old with a win over 5f on soft; by nature a prominent racer, but with the berths behind Rosie Frith already full, Seamie Heffernan will likely find this horse forced to race at a position it does not naturally occupy, tempering its winning prospects.

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.note: Stablemate of Cardiff By The Sea, also trained by Stack and equally a horse that prefers to race close to the pace; Gavin Ryan rides, fresh off a run seven days ago, but the same congestion issue that affects Cardiff By The Sea applies here — its chance is contingent on finding a gap from a non-ideal starting position.

runners_data.name: Rosie Frith
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner; Shane Foley has a straightforward tactical job with two wins at 5f on good-to-yielding in recent history, and uncontested access to the lead on yielding ground at Cork over the minimum trip represents an optimal scenario for this three-year-old.

runners_data.name: Xerling
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides this three-year-old who won at 5f on good recently and has placed twice at the trip; a prominent runner who will be fighting for position from the break, and the form trajectory (0-2-1-2-0 in reverse) is mixed, though the 5f trip on similar going is squarely in range.

races.paceDynamic: Rosie Frith is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Shane Foley can control tempo from the front at a pace that suits her rather than her rivals — on Good to Yielding at Cork over 5f, that is likely to be a honest but manageable gallop rather than a suicidal sprint. Four runners — Kendall Roy, Brussels, Likedbymike, and Xerling — all want to race prominently, meaning the positions directly behind Rosie Frith will be intensely contested from the off, creating significant traffic friction between the 2f and 3f poles where the field begins to compress on the run to the line. Cardiff By The Sea and Focaccia are both natural prominent types who are mapped to midfield purely because the prominent berths are already oversubscribed; neither is a genuine hold-up horse and their redistribution to midfield means their winning chance depends on threading through a congested pack. This race shape — a single uncontested leader, a scrappy fight for the positions behind, and soft-ground conditions that reward economical travel — strongly favours the front-runner profile and those able to track smoothly just off the pace, while true hold-up horses are disadvantaged by a field unlikely to set up a meaningful closing run. Cardiff By The Sea and Focaccia are the two most likely to be pushed out of their natural position; of the genuine prominent runners, Kendall Roy and Likedbymike are best placed to actually secure a position on Rosie Frith's quarters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rosie Frith Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Rosie Frith gets a clean break and dictates an uncontested, measured pace that dries up late finishing kicks on the yielding ground.
scenarios.body: Rosie Frith, twice a winner at 5f on good-to-yielding and fresh off a strong recent run, simply builds an advantage the prominent pack cannot peg back through the final furlong with no pace-pressure to force her to over-race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmage behind Rosie Frith produces a clean-travelling tracker who pounces inside the final furlong as the leader ties up slightly on the testing ground.
scenarios.body: The yielding conditions at Cork place a premium on horses who travel economically within their pace, and a prominent runner who avoids the early traffic chaos and settles just off Rosie Frith's shoulder is ideally positioned to cut her down late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Storms
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent battle behind Rosie Frith is unusually fierce and creates enough pace to burn out the leaders, leaving the race open for a late sweep from deeper.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on the genuine hold-up types — Erosandpsyche, Gazelle d'Or, Sarahmae — getting a strong enough pace to chase, which is possible but against the dominant race shape; Sarahmae's 5f form on soft is the most relevant profile here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage Flattens Field
scenarios.trigger: If the four-way battle for prominent positions produces sustained interference and multiple horses lose their action at the critical 2f point, scrambling the result unpredictably.
scenarios.body: In this chaotic scenario any horse that sidesteps the trouble — potentially Cardiff By The Sea or Focaccia if they find a gap from their forced midfield berth — could benefit, though their out-of-role positioning means this is a low-probability fluke outcome rather than a structured winning shape.

watchPoints.text: Rosie Frith — watch the break: if she exits the stalls cleanly she secures an uncontested lead, but any stumble hands the tactical control to the four-horse prominent pack behind her and changes the entire race shape.

Kendall Roy, Brussels, Likedbymike, Xerling — all four want the same prominent positions, and the 2f-to-3f zone on the run to the line is where traffic friction is most likely to cost one or more of them the race; watch which, if any, gets a clean passage.

Cardiff By The Sea and Focaccia — both Stack-trained horses are natural prominent types forced into midfield by the congested pace map; if either finds a gap early and motors into their preferred position, the published race shape will be wrong and their chance upgrades sharply.

Gazelle d'Or — the 86-day absence is notable for a hold-up specialist who needs everything to fall right; M C Grassick runners returning from a break of this length should be monitored in the market for any significant move that might indicate stable confidence.

Sarahmae — the only hold-up horse with a confirmed win on soft/yielding at 5f in recent form; if the Cork ground is riding closer to yielding than good, this horse's profile becomes relatively more interesting even in a pace shape that does not naturally suit it.

races.name: Cork Maiden

runners_data.name: Carry The Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who faded finishing eighth on their only start over a mile on Soft at Dundalk; drops to six furlongs here but the tendency to fade is a concern in a big-field maiden where getting a clear run from the back is never guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Hurleys Hill
runners_data.note: Finished eleventh on debut over seven furlongs Soft and was beaten a long way; the hold-up profile compounds the challenge in a 17-runner race where cover is hard to find and the finishing tendency is also flagged as a concern.

runners_data.name: Inform
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant trained by G M Lyons, who has a formidable T14 record of 4/23; Colin Keane is a strong booking and this yard regularly produce debut winners — the complete unknown going profile means this runner must be treated as a serious threat.

runners_data.name: Keogie
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has placed twice at six furlongs including a second at Dundalk on Soft-going, giving genuine relevance here on Good to Yielding; 106 days off is a query but Noel Meade is capable of producing a fresh horse ready to run and the trip profile fits.

runners_data.name: Noble Irish
runners_data.note: Debut runner for A P O'Brien with Wayne Lordan booked — a powerful combination in any maiden; going and style entirely unknown but the stable's debutants over six furlongs at Cork demand respect without form to oppose.

runners_data.name: Optics
runners_data.note: Finished sixth, seventh, and thirteenth in three starts and has struggled in similar company; a genuine hold-up type whose natural position is at the rear, which is challenging in a 17-runner field — the redistribution to midfield on the map reflects crowding, not a change in how this horse actually races, and its chance is further tempered by racing out of role.

runners_data.name: Spider Star
runners_data.note: Unraced debut runner for David Harry Kelly with Andrew Slattery; the trainer has a respectable T14 strike rate of 4/13 and this is a yard that can produce competitive debutants, though the complete absence of form makes assessment difficult.

runners_data.name: Spinola Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has finished seventh and seventeenth in two runs on Good going over six and seven furlongs; form is discouraging and no wins or placings to point to, though both runs have come on similar going which at least confirms suitability for conditions.

runners_data.name: Faithful Ardad
runners_data.note: Trainer Kieran P Cotter, no T14 form to speak of, and Declan McDonogh booked for what appears to be a debut or near-debut run; unknown going and style profile means this is an entirely speculative entry until more is known.

runners_data.name: Feel Happy
runners_data.note: Consistent placing type who has finished fourth, sixth, and fourth in her three runs across good and soft ground, always hitting the frame without winning; Donnacha A O'Brien yard in fair recent form and the six-furlong trip on today's going is within her range, though a win remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Grande Cuvee
runners_data.note: Prominent runner placed twice at five furlongs on good and Soft ground before finishing ninth stepping up to six furlongs on Soft for J A Stack; the step back to a stronger pace scenario here over six could suit if she gets a prominent berth, and Seamie Heffernan is a high-quality booking.

runners_data.name: Haroussa
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for J P Murtagh who has finished fifth and ninth over a mile on Good going; the drop to six furlongs is a significant trip shortening and Ben Coen takes the ride — it remains to be seen whether the sharper speed required suits, though the going is fine.

runners_data.name: Lilli's Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has finished eighth and ninth in two runs on Good going at six and seven furlongs; the fading tendency is flagged and the form gives little encouragement, though conditions are familiar.

runners_data.name: Otsana
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed front-runners, finished fifth over seven furlongs Good on debut; drops to six furlongs which should sharpen the trip up and W J Lee gets the ride for P Twomey — dictating from the front over a shorter trip is the clear angle here.

runners_data.name: Red Dahlia
runners_data.note: Debut runner for John Joseph Murphy with Shane Foley in the saddle — a strong jockey booking that always demands attention in an Irish maiden; going and style entirely unknown so assessment is speculative, but Foley's presence keeps this runner in the conversation.

runners_data.name: Saint Agatha
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner, returned a long way off (118 days) having placed twice including a second over seven furlongs Good; drops to six furlongs and her front-running profile should see her in the mix from the outset with Gavin Ryan riding.

runners_data.name: She's Too Kool
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a consistent recent profile — placed at six furlongs on Good ground twice, with five of her eight runs at this trip on similar going; the volume of hold-up types in this field makes getting a clear run difficult, but the track-record at the trip on this going is her key asset.

races.paceDynamic: Otsana and Saint Agatha are the two confirmed front-runners in a 17-runner maiden, and both will be pressing for the rail and an early advantage on the Good to Yielding ground at Cork over six furlongs. With only two genuine pace-setters in a big field, the early gallop will be honest rather than suicidal — they will stride clear of the pack but without the kind of burning tempo that would inevitably see them fold, meaning the race is set to be run at a rhythm that could genuinely reward those who travel up close. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, with Optics a true hold-up runner shuffled into a midfield depiction because of the volume of closers; the runners most likely to actually secure prominent berths behind the two leaders are Keogie, Haroussa, and Grande Cuvee given their natural prominent profiles. Tactical verdict: this race shape — two clear front-runners, honest pace, big field — sets up ideally for prominent-to-midfield stalkers who can track the gallop without using up energy fighting for position early, and those settled just behind the leaders will have first run on a track where positional advantage matters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Leaders Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners Otsana and Saint Agatha control the pace without being harried and the honest gallop on Good to Yielding ground suits both to sustain their effort to the line.
scenarios.body: With no third front-runner to force the tempo beyond their comfort zone, either Otsana or Saint Agatha could dictate at a manageable clip and find enough reserves to hold on, particularly over a relatively short six furlongs where leading types often don't fully capitulate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Otsana and Saint Agatha is genuinely honest but not excessive, allowing horses racing prominently just behind to track and pounce in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Keogie has placed twice at six furlongs and goes well on this type of ground, while Haroussa and Grande Cuvee both have prominent styles and the experience to slot in close to the pace and deliver a challenge; the big field creates scrimmage risks that punish those further back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Improver Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the several lightly raced, unraced or unknown-going runners — Inform, Noble Irish, Spider Star, Faithful Ardad, or Red Dahlia — turns out to be well above maiden company and lands a debut or near-debut win on a potentially lenient mark.
scenarios.body: Colin Keane on Inform (G M Lyons yard, strong T14 strike rate) and Wayne Lordan on Noble Irish (A P O'Brien) represent the two most dangerous unknown quantities in this scenario, with both stables capable of producing a well-prepared debutant ready to win; the open nature of the form book means this scenario remains live despite the uncertainty.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace from Otsana and Saint Agatha is stronger than anticipated and the field strings out, allowing genuine hold-up types to come through beaten horses in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: She's Too Kool has multiple placed efforts at six furlongs on good ground and has shown consistent form without winning, while Feel Happy has placed at this trip before; however, with Optics racing out of role and the redistribution of hold-up types meaning the true finishers are fewer than they appear, this scenario is the least likely to deliver.

watchPoints.text: Otsana and Saint Agatha will both look to cross to the rail immediately — watch for a bump or crowding at the start that disrupts either front-runner's rhythm, which could cascade through the tightly packed 17-runner field.

Inform (G M Lyons, Colin Keane) and Noble Irish (A P O'Brien, Wayne Lordan) are both unknown quantities on debut — if either is well fancied in the market it signals insider confidence that could make them a major price threat.

Keogie has been off 106 days and drops sharply back in trip; watch the pre-race market for signs of market support — if the Meade yard has her fit and ready, her placed form at six furlongs on this going makes her a live prominent player.

With 17 runners on Good to Yielding ground, the draw and early position battle will be critical — horses drawn wide who get squeezed at the break could find themselves detached from the main group before the race has settled.

Grande Cuvee and Haroussa both have prominent profiles but were placed at five furlongs and over a mile respectively — watch whether either can adapt to the six-furlong speed demands in a contest where the pace shape is honest from the front.

races.name: Follow Us On Instagram Handicap

runners_data.name: Arch Enemy
runners_data.note: Hold-up galloper with two wins over 12f on Good ground (form: 1/12f/GOO twice); 29 days fresh and in consistent form, but a 21-runner field with a hot pace means a clear run cannot be guaranteed for Sam Coen (5lb claimer) coming from the rear.

runners_data.name: Forlio
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type; W J Lee rides for the in-form Paul Flynn stable (T14: 1/20) and the horse has a win at 12f on Good ground, but his 19f and 16f efforts in the last two starts suggest stamina extension is no concern — real pace needed ahead to bring him into it late.

runners_data.name: Glittering Gem
runners_data.note: Weld-trained 4yo with Chris Hayes in the saddle, a potent combination; styles himself as a prominent racer and showed 2P in recent outings at 10-12f on Good, and the step to 1m4f on Good To Yielding looks tailor-made — the ideal pace-on shape here.

runners_data.name: Louiescall
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has competed over 16f multiple times and won at that trip; trainer David Harry Kelly is in excellent form (T14: 4/13) and at 14 days since last run he arrives fresh — primary pacer to lead and a real chance to control the race from the front.

runners_data.name: Justenzia
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a mixed record; only one win in the last 15 starts and tends to finish mid-pack; the sheer volume of hold-up types in this race and a 31-day break make securing any tactical advantage difficult despite Good To Yielding suiting on paper.

runners_data.name: Morse
runners_data.note: Drops back from 80 days off for Charles Weld; form flagged as fading in finish, which is a significant concern in a strongly-run 1m4f stamina test — the layoff and fade tendency make this a speculative proposition even though the hold-up style could theoretically suit a strong pace.

runners_data.name: Victoria Kesia
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who operates over extreme trips (16-18f mostly); dropping to 1m4f is a reduction in trip and may not see her at her best, despite the form showing a placed effort at 18f on Good — the trip is shorter than her optimal range.

runners_data.name: Dutch Gold
runners_data.note: True hold-up runner whose natural style is deepest closer; 69 days absent and fade tendency noted in form — the redistribution to mid-pack reflects how many closers this field contains, and his chance depends entirely on a truly punishing pace fully clearing out the leaders.

runners_data.name: Questionable
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer displaced to midfield on the map by weight of closers in this field; tongue tie worn, 54 days off, and best form at 10-12f on Good — the 14f trip is a query and positional competition from other closers means carving a run late will be difficult.

runners_data.name: Valjean
runners_data.note: Returned from 682 days off — by far the longest layoff in the field; Charles Weld horses often need a run after such an absence and the headgear (hood) is worth noting; he is a hold-up type whose chance is slim on comeback fitness grounds alone regardless of style.

runners_data.name: Rocket Robyn
runners_data.note: Young 4yo filly whose best form is at shorter trips (7-10f); she fades in finish and the redistribution reflects that genuine stayers dominate the rear of this field — the step up to 1m4f Good To Yielding looks too much given she has never placed beyond 10f.

runners_data.name: Eternal Echo
runners_data.note: Carry a string of unplaced efforts at 13-16f on Good; the redistribution captures that she is squeezed into midfield rather than her natural rear position; Seamie Heffernan is an upgrade in quality but two unfinished (U) runs and inconsistent form make her difficult to trust.

runners_data.name: Guy's Girl
runners_data.note: 4yo trained by McCreery (T14: 3/13, good form), and her best run was a 3rd over 13f on Good — a relevant effort; she is a natural hold-up type crowded to midfield on the map, and will need a stronger pace than usual to pick up late against rivals with more stamina scope.

runners_data.name: Nancee Spain
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a win at 12f on Soft and blinkers on — headgear confirms she needs to be kept focused up front; form over 14f twice suggests she handles the trip, but she has never led against this level of pace competition and may not last home.

runners_data.name: Ohmali
runners_data.note: Hold-up 4yo whose best effort was a 2nd over 8f on Good; the step to 1m4f looks a significant stamina leap and she has shown no form beyond 11f — squeezed to midfield on the map, her chance depends on a trip she is yet to prove she stays.

runners_data.name: Preparations
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on Good last time out and trainer Andrew Slattery is in flying form (T14: 3/19); naturally a hold-up type but the redistribution to midfield captures the crowding — Jimmy Dalton (7lb) keeps the weight competitive and he's proven over the trip.

runners_data.name: Out On Friday
runners_data.note: Third confirmed front-runner in the race, a 10-year-old veteran ridden by Wesley Joyce (3lb); has form at 12-14f and tends to press on, but at this age and in this company against two younger pacemakers, burning out before the straight is a real risk.

runners_data.name: Lauderdale King
runners_data.note: 4yo trained by Slattery with progressive profile (3rd, 4th, 5th in recent starts); hold-up style naturally but placed mid-pack on the map because the field is over-subscribed with closers — his form is improving and Andrew Slattery takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Beauvallon
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the race (OR=71) from the Mullins stable without a jockey listed but clearly the class act; form shows 2W at 16f on Good/Soft, making the 1m4f on Good To Yielding within range — natural hold-up runner whose class and stamina make him a prime candidate if the pace delivers.

runners_data.name: Charlie Brow'n
runners_data.note: Won at 14f on Soft and ran 3rd at 14f on Good — directly relevant form for this contest; a natural hold-up type redistributed to midfield, trainer O'Mara has a modest strike rate (T14: 0/4) but the horse's course-and-distance profile is one of the strongest in the field.

runners_data.name: Miss Australie
runners_data.note: Won at 14f on Good just 3 days ago — an extremely quick return, which is notable; Adrian McGuinness is highly active (T14: 4/24) and the horse is proven at the trip, but racing back this fast on Good To Yielding after a win raises a fitness query. Natural hold-up type placed in midfield on the map.

races.paceDynamic: Louiescall, Nancee Spain, and Out On Friday are all confirmed front-runners in a 21-runner 1m4f handicap on Good To Yielding ground at Cork, guaranteeing a strong, unrelenting gallop from the outset with genuine three-way pace pressure throughout. The honest tempo over this trip on soft-ish ground will stretch the field early, pile stamina pressure on the leaders, and create a race that sets up classically for horses able to travel prominently without expending energy fighting for position. Glittering Gem (D.K. Weld, Chris Hayes) is the standout prominent type who can sit just off the pace without scrambling, while Beauvallon and Arch Enemy are genuine hold-up candidates. The field contains a surplus of true hold-up types — Dutch Gold, Valjean, Questionable, Rocket Robyn, Eternal Echo, Ohmali, Preparations, Lauderdale King, Guy's Girl, Charlie Brow'n, and Miss Australie are all redistribution-mapped to midfield, but the natural leaders will push them back regardless; only those with genuine positional flexibility will benefit. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses racing prominently just off a contested lead — those who can switch off in second or third and pick off weakening front-runners in the final two furlongs — meaning prominent and high-midfield gallopers with stamina and class are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Suits Prominent Stalkers
scenarios.trigger: If Louiescall, Nancee Spain, and Out On Friday burn each other off setting a strong honest gallop, the race is set up perfectly for a prominent racer to stalk and pounce.
scenarios.body: The three leaders battle through the first mile, leaving a prominent runner travelling sweetly in second or third best-placed to pick them up entering the straight; the Good To Yielding ground extends the stamina test further and rewards those with class and relentless galloping ability. Glittering Gem, trained by the masterful D.K. Weld and ridden by Chris Hayes, is the archetypal beneficiary, while Beauvallon's 2W3P form over 16f+ suits this shaping perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Strong Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pacemakers — most likely Louiescall — settles better than the others and dictates a controlled but brisk tempo, stealing a decisive advantage.
scenarios.body: Louiescall has strong 1m4f-2m form and a trainer in David Harry Kelly who is firing (T14: 4/13), and if he breaks cleanly and imposes himself fractionally ahead of Nancee Spain and Out On Friday he could dictate terms and have enough in reserve to hold on. The Good To Yielding ground suits his form profile and he has won at today's trip, making him the most credible leader to survive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Grind Suits Deep Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly brutal and burns off even the prominent stalkers, leaving a late-running stayer to come through beaten horses in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Beauvallon (Mullins yard, 2W at 16f+ on similar ground) is the most credible genuine closer, with a form profile pointing squarely at this scenario, while Arch Enemy has won twice over this trip on Good ground and could finish powerfully if given a clear run. The redistribution caveat applies to most other hold-up runners, making this a narrower outcome than the raw number of closers in the field might suggest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Aids Tactical Runners
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners check each other early and the pace is less fierce than expected, allowing a tactical mid-division runner to win without being fully tested on stamina.
scenarios.body: In a softer gallop, Glittering Gem's pace and Preparations' recent win form (1/12f/GOO) could see them dictate the finish on ability rather than raw stamina; however this outcome is least likely given three genuine leaders rarely settle for a moderate tempo. Forlio and Miss Australie, both recent winners at the trip, carry each-way claims in this scenario if the pace collapses.

watchPoints.text: Beauvallon (Mullins, OR 71) is the class runner in the field with two wins over 16f at similar going — watch whether he gets a clear run from the rear in a 21-runner field, as a trouble-free passage would make him a serious danger to all.

The three-way pace battle between Louiescall, Nancee Spain, and Out On Friday could collapse into a scramble from the two-furlong pole — watch which leader is weakening first, as it signals the front end burning out and the prominent stalkers' chance arriving.
